text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kerio South Member of Parliament (MP) Nicholas Biwott and controversial Cherangani MP Kipruto arap Kirwa emerge as the main beneficiaries in the thorough government shake-up announced by President Daniel arap Moi on Wednesday.

- The major reshuffle made by President Moi will be interpreted by many observers as a decisive score by the ruling party's Kenya African National Union's (KANU) so-called Kanu "B" group in the ongoing Moi succession struggle. The "B" group favours Vice-President George Saitoti as Moi successor.
- Police Commissioner Duncan Wachira stops mounting of permanent roadblocks saying they have become illegal toll stations.
- Dairy farmers in Bomet district, Rift Valley, welcome the sacking of Kipkalya Kones as minister in presidency, saying he had constantly frustrated and antagonised them.
- High Court allows main opposition FORD-Kenya party chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa to go ahead and hold the party's National Delegates Congress on January 25 and 26.
- A lack of a national shipping fleet has affected employment opportunities in Kenya maritime industry, experts in the industry's labour standards said.
- Police in the western town of Kakamega launch a manhunt for a group of four youths who abducted two school girls.
- An Assistant Minister for Labour Mohamed Ali says a job racket perpetrated by fake recruitment agents is ripping off Kenyans for millions of shillings annually.
